messages:
Sam: Heads up — perf-bot flagged a +12% p99 regression on mistral-7b AWQ int4 after yesterday's kernel selector tweak.
perf-bot: [automation] Regression detected: mistral-7b AWQ int4; p99 +12% latency; sample dims: batch=8 seq=512 heads=32 kv_dim=64. CI link: https://ci.internal/runs/8923
Maya: ack. I ran a quick profile. Looks like the gather kernel is falling back to a slower path when heads*kv_dim isn't 64-aligned. trace snippet: ```kernel: matmul_gather_fp16 -> fallback_slow_gemv
batcher: microbatch=1 -> dynbatch enabled```
Sam: any idea why this started after the selector change? selector should've preferred the fast kernel.
Izzy: The selector heuristic uses alignment + ropescale heuristics. With rope_scale=0.9 the effective stride distribution changed and we now hit a non-aligned codepath for some layers. Also AWQ calibration prompts produce longer instruction prefixes which shift seq-length util distribution.
Jules: I can repro on mixtral-8b too, but only for AWQ calibrations (long system+user prompts). Latency hit ~15-20% and small accuracy delta (~0.6% BLEU).
Maya: Proposal: for AWQ on GPUs with fp8 support, prefer the prefetch-friendly fallback kernel and enable batched_kv_prefetch rather than forcing strict alignment. Quick patch idea: ```if (model.quant == "AWQ" && gpu.has_fp8) prefer_prefetch=true;```
Sam: let's A/B on dedicated rigs before changing the selector globally. Can you run v2-lite selector vs v2? I can allocate capacity.
Izzy: kicked off jobs (dedicated pool): job 1745612360 = selector=v2-lite, job 1745612370 = selector=v2. Will monitor.
perf-bot: Job 1745612360 finished: p99=218ms, p50=38ms, tokens/sec +3%. Job 1745612370 finished: p99=250ms, p50=36ms, tokens/sec baseline. Accuracy diffs within 0.1% for our eval set.
Sam: clear win for v2-lite on AWQ + mixtral/mistral families. Let's canary roll v2-lite for AWQ models and add a telemetry flag to gate rope_scale<1.0. I'll open an RFC and a rollout plan.
Jules: I'll curate a reproducible calibration prompt set (long-codegen, system+user long) to make the accuracy delta deterministic. Attaching to the RFC.
Maya: FYI saw kv-cache eviction spike at seq=2048 when dynbatch enabled on the same runs — might be unrelated but worth watching (eviction churn increases latency variance).
Sam: Great catch. Add an observability alert on kv-evict-rate for dynbatch-enabled pools. Thanks all :thumbsup:
